explanation:
[EFFECT] The hour of the day has a strongly non-monotonic effect on predicted bike demand. Contributions are deeply negative in the early morning hours (roughly midnight to 5 AM), reaching their lowest point around 4 AM — meaning demand is predicted to be at its smallest then. Contributions then rise sharply, producing two distinct peaks: a morning peak around 8 AM and a larger evening peak around 5–6 PM (hour 17–18, SHAP value ≈ +1.0), after which demand falls off again through the late evening.

[IMPORTANCE] Hour of the day is the single most important feature in the model, ranked 1st out of 9 with an importance score of 0.833. Its influence on predicted demand is far greater than any other feature, dwarfing the effects of weather, temperature, or season.

[RECOMMENDATION] Staff and bike availability should be concentrated around the two daily demand peaks — the morning commute (~8 AM) and especially the evening commute (~5–6 PM) — while overnight hours (roughly 1–5 AM) can be used for maintenance and rebalancing with minimal disruption to riders.
